title: Geo-harmonized routing and resilient streaming sessions for hosted API
creator: Lena Chen
description: Goal: Implement a geo-harmonized, session-cohesive failover strategy for the hosted API gateway that preserves streaming session continuity where possible, and provides deterministic graceful degradation (load shedding and circuit breakers) when region capacity is constrained. This ticket covers design, implementation, and rollout of: 1) per-region SLO enforcement and budgeted failover triggers; 2) L7 routing rules with session affinity and KV-backed session continuation tokens; 3) streaming-aware fallback behavior that can degrade to polling or truncated streams; 4) region-level circuit breakers and adaptive load shedding based on latency/error budgets. The end-state should keep most customer sessions alive during partial region outages, avoid cascading latency spikes, and provide measurable SLO spend accounting for failover events.
problem_statement: We currently route hosted API traffic using a global L7 edge with health checks and simple weight-based failover. This causes two recurring problems: (1) long-lived streaming sessions often drop or restart when traffic shifts between regions because state (session position, prefix KV cache pointers, open SSE/TCP streams) is not portable across gateways; (2) region overload causes latency tails and cascading failures across downstream subsystems before we can safely shed load. We need a resilient flow that preserves session continuity where feasible and degrades predictably otherwise, without violating customer SLO commitments or incurring undue cost.
proposed_solution: High-level design: 1) SLO and budget model: define per-region SLOs (p50/p95/p99 latency and error-rate) and an explicit Failover Budget token that is decremented when we route requests to non-primary regions. The Failover Budget ties to each customer/tenant and to global platform budgets so we can control cross-customer blast radius. 2) Routing plane: implement a geo-harmonized router component in the edge that uses: - primary region mapping (by geolocation + latency matrix) - consistent hashing-based session affinity for non-stream requests - session tokens for streaming: issue a signed session-continuation-token (SCT) at stream start that encodes the minimal state (KV pointers, prefix checksum, model variant) and can be used to rehydrate the session in another region. Tokens are HMAC-signed and short-lived. 3) Streaming continuity: support two modes: sticky-stream (try to keep stream on original region via sticky routing and long HA keepalives) and portable-stream (if original region unavailable, accept SCT to pick up near last delivered token; if full-consistency can't be met, fallback to best-effort resume or to a truncated/polling mode with clear response headers indicating degraded continuity). 4) Circuit breakers & load-shedding: per-region breakers based on composite signals (95th latency, 5xx rate, queue length, GPU utilization). Breakers have three states: closed, throttled (soft shed by returning 429 with suggested backoff), and open (fast fail and route to fallback region/variant). Load-shedding policies prefer shedding non-critical work types first: embeddings batch jobs, lower-priority tenants, heavy long-context generation, then chat completions. 5) Telemetry & observability: dashboards for SLO spend, per-tenant failover counts, streaming resume success rate, and per-region breaker triggers. 6) Rollout: feature flags, canary to low-volume tenants, emergency off ramp.
technical_details: Routing mechanics: - Use a global L7 control plane that publishes per-region weight tables and affinity rules to edge routers. - Session affinity uses consistent hashing on session_id or API key + client_ip as a fallback. - For streaming, at stream creation the origin gateway stores minimal pointers to prefix/KV cache entries (opaque IDs) and returns an SCT. The origin also checkpoint-stores the last delivered token index in a short-lived replication log that is replicated to the nearest secondary region cluster with eventual consistency (replication window <= 10s). - SCT format: base64(hdr.payload.signature) where payload includes model_id, variant, prefix_checksum, last_token_index, origin_region, issuance_ts. Signature HMAC using account-level secret. - When a rehydrate occurs, the target region validates SCT, checks for compatible model variants, and rehydrates KV pointers; if pointers missing, we can replay a truncated prompt constructed from the last known prefix checksum and send a warning header to client. - Health signals: integrate runtime telemetry (rt_latency_p95, rpc_5xx_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate, gpu_queued_ms). Composite breaker expression: open_if(rt_latency_p95 > 3xSLO_p95 OR rpc_5xx_rate > 0.02) with manual tuning knobs per region. - Failover decision: incremental policy that prefers local mitigation (throttle, cache bypass, quantized model fallback) before cross-region shift to avoid extra latency tax and SLO spend. - Load-shedding actions must be observable and annotatable per response (headers: X-Redwood-Fallback, X-Redwood-SCT-Status, X-Redwood-Shed-Reason).
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Complexity: Introducing SCTs and cross-region replication increases code and operational complexity. - Consistency vs availability: portable-stream requires eventual replication and may still lose a small window of in-flight tokens. We accept bounded loss (<= configurable tokens) for availability. - Cost: replicating checkpoints to secondaries and routing extra traffic during failovers consumes cross-region bandwidth and compute. We mitigate via Failover Budget limits and prioritized tenant lists. - Security: SCTs carry session metadata; must be short-lived, signed, and audited. Storing per-session pointers requires lifecycle management to avoid data retention issues. - Edge cases: model variant unavailability in fallback region — we need to degrade model quality gracefully or apply deterministic fallback variants with documented semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Per-region SLOs and Failover Budget documented and implemented in control plane
Edge router can issue and validate SCTs and route streaming rehydrates successfully in test harness
Circuit breakers trigger and transition through states in response to synthetic load tests
Load-shedding order respects priority table and emits clear headers and metrics
Canary rollout to 5% of traffic shows <2% increase in client-observed disconnects and >80% successful stream resume on cross-region rehydrate
Dashboards show SLO spend and per-tenant failover counts; alerts for unexpected failover spikes
implementation_steps: Design and document SCT format and security model (Confluence link in links)
Add SCT issuance to streaming pathway and minimal checkpointing in gateway runtime
Extend control plane to publish affinity and failover budget state to edges
Implement per-region composite circuit breakers and soft-shed responses
Add server-side replay/rehydrate logic in secondary region that accepts SCTs
Create telemetry dashboards and SLO spend metrics; add alerts
Canary rollout and iterative tuning based on metrics and customer feedback

incident_playbook: Step 0: Identify region degradation via composite breaker alert. Step 1: Shift failsafe to soft-throttle for affected region. Step 2: If still degrading, enable cross-region failover for affected tenants within Failover Budget. Step 3: Notify SRE and toggle canary off if unexplained errors. Step 4: Post-incident runbook: capture SLO spend and update global budget policies.
